title: Private VPC ARP storm during agent upgrade - retrospective and action items
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: During a rolling upgrade of the private agent in several customer VPCs, we observed a brief but severe control-plane connectivity outage caused by an ARP broadcast storm and duplicate MAC advertisements from updated agents. This caused BGP neighbors in affected tenants to flap and NAT gateway ARP caches to saturate, resulting in ~8-12 minutes of degraded API traffic for a subset of customers. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied during the incident, and follow-up action items.
timeline: 2026-02-10 02:12 UTC - Automated rolling upgrade started for private-agent v3.7.2 across region-us-west-2 tenants.
2026-02-10 02:14 UTC - First alerts: control-plane telemetry from 3 tenants showed increased connection resets and higher retransmits.
2026-02-10 02:18 UTC - NetworkOps observed elevated ARP request rates on affected VPCs; NAT gateways reported ARP table thrash and eviction logs.
2026-02-10 02:20 UTC - Engine team paused the rolling upgrade at 12% completion after pattern confirmed across multiple tenants.
2026-02-10 02:30 UTC - Emergency hotfix deployed to upgrade script to stagger interface re-attachment and disable gratuitous ARP emission from agent startup.
2026-02-10 02:34 UTC - Control-plane connectivity recovered for most tenants; full rollback avoided. Post-incident monitoring run for two hours.
2026-02-10 03:10 UTC - Upgrade safely resumed with staggered windows and additional rate-limits; completed without recurrence.
root_cause: The upgraded private agent (v3.7.2) changed its network initialization sequence to rebind interfaces and announce its overlay MAC immediately via gratuitous ARP packets. When the upgrade ran across many hosts in a tenant without sufficient staggering, NAT gateway and VPC ARP caches experienced sudden churn. The combination of short ARP cache timers on some cloud NAT instances and a prior config change that reduced ARP cache size (rollout ENG-517203) caused cache eviction loops. Evicted entries forced repeated ARP queries, amplifying broadcast traffic and triggering BGP neighbor instability in a subset of customers where control-plane paths traverse the same virtual networks.
contributing_factors: Agent startup now sends gratuitous ARP to accelerate flow steering (changed in v3.7.2) without rollout coordination.
Recent NAT/edge config change (ENG-517203) reduced ARP table thresholds in certain cloud regions.
Rolling upgrade orchestration did not enforce tenant-level staggering; multiple agents in same tenant were upgraded concurrently.
Insufficient observability for ARP/Layer-2 metrics in the console; alerts were tied to control-plane RPC errors rather than network broadcast metrics.
No preflight upgrade simulation against low-ARP-capacity topologies in the private deployment test harness.
mitigations_during_incident: Paused automatic rollout at 12% and prevented further agent restarts in affected regions.
Applied an emergency patch to the agent startup to temporarily suppress gratuitous ARP emission.
Staggered remaining upgrades with tenant-aware windows (max 1 host per tenant per 15 minutes).
Requested cloud provider support to temporarily increase ARP cache size on impacted NAT gateways where feasible.
long_term_action_items: (Owner: NetEng / Due: 2026-03-03) Add a preflight network model test to the private-deploy CI that simulates agent restarts against constrained ARP table sizes and verifies no broadcast amplification.
(Owner: Orchestration / Due: 2026-02-24) Implement tenant-aware upgrade scheduling in the rollout controller so that agents within the same VPC/tenant are never restarted concurrently.
(Owner: Agents / Due: 2026-02-28) Revert gratuitous ARP by default and expose a gated config flag; require explicit opt-in and rollout plan to enable accelerated flow steering.

(Owner: Observability / Due: 2026-02-21) Instrument Layer-2 metrics (ARP request rate, gratuitous ARP count, interface flaps) into the Console; add an alert rule for ARP>threshold that maps to an internal network incident runbook.
(Owner: Platform / Due: 2026-03-10) Add a pre-merge upgrade impact checklist for changes that touch agent networking stack (must include low-ARP-capacity test and orchestration impact assessment).
(Owner: Support / Due: 2026-02-20) Create a customer-facing incident summary template for private deployment connectivity incidents and add to runbook.
resolution: We prevented a full rollback by pausing the upgrade and deploying a hotfix to suppress gratuitous ARP. The remainder of the rollout completed with tenant-aware staggering. No persistent data loss occurred. We will implement the long-term items above before re-enabling gratuitous ARP in default agent images.
comments: Asha Menon (2026-02-10): Observed the same ARP churn in our internal testbed when simulating 80% tenant concurrency; we should add that scenario to CI.
Liam Chen (2026-02-10): Paused rollout and pushed hotfix to suppress gratuitous ARP. Followed up with provider to increase ARP table temporarily.
Marta Ruiz (2026-02-11): Raised that ENG-517203 reduced ARP thresholds; scheduling a rollback of that config change for impacted regions as a precaution.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-16): Drafted tenant-aware scheduler design doc and linked in postmortem. Need review from NetEng and Orchestration.
Customer Success (2026-02-12): Notified 6 impacted customers with mitigation summary and ETA for fixes; no SLA credits yet, monitoring for follow-ups.
next_steps_meeting: 2026-02-18 16:00 UTC internal review (NetEng, Agents, Orchestration, Observability, Support) - agenda: finalize tenant-aware scheduler spec, confirm ARP metrics, assign owners for implementation. Calendar invite sent.
notes: Do not re-enable gratuitous ARP in agent release stream until CI tests and orchestration changes are in place. Consider adding a canary that limits upgrades to single-tenant per rollout by default for next two releases.
